Privacy Policy

Last updated 7 November 2026

Ultron is a voice assistant for Android made by Jitin Kumar Sengar. This page explains what data Ultron handles, where it goes, and the choices you have. If anything is unclear, write to devxjitin@gmail.com.

The short version

  • Your memories, conversation history, documents and usage numbers are stored on your phone.
  • To talk and think, Ultron sends what you say, and the information needed to answer, to Google Gemini using your own Gemini API key.
  • We keep the name, email and phone number you give when you buy, and the status of your activation key, so we can deliver and support it.
  • We do not sell your data and we do not show ads.

What stays on your phone

  • Saved memories and the history of your conversations.
  • Documents you add to the knowledge base, and the search index made from them.
  • Your skills, your settings, and usage numbers such as talk time.
  • Your Gemini API key, encrypted with Android’s keystore.

This data does not leave the phone unless a feature you use needs it, as described below. You can clear it in the app under Storage, or by uninstalling Ultron.

What is sent to Google Gemini

Ultron uses your own Gemini API key, so Google handles this data under its own terms and privacy policy, and the key is your account with Google. Depending on what you ask, this can include:

  • Your voice and the words you say, during a live conversation.
  • The results of tools you enable, for example contacts, calendar events, location, clipboard, file names, app usage, notifications, or the text on your screen when you ask Ultron to read it.
  • A screenshot, when you ask Ultron to look at the screen.
  • Text from documents you add to the knowledge base, which is sent to create search embeddings.
  • Past conversation snippets or memories, when you ask about something you said earlier.

Tools that read personal data are off until you connect them in the app and grant the Android permission yourself. Ultron treats web pages, messages and tool output as data, not as instructions.

What we keep to run your key

When you buy a plan, you give us your name, email address and phone number. We store them with your activation key so we can email the key, support you, move the key to a new phone and keep track of its plan and expiry. Alongside that we store:

  • A one-way hash of the key (not the key itself), its plan, the amount you paid, and when it was created, emailed, activated and when it expires.
  • An anonymous account identifier for the phone the key is activated on, and when it last moved.

The activation email is sent through Resend, an email delivery service, which handles your name and email address only to deliver that message. These records are kept on Amazon Web Services while your key is active and for as long afterwards as we need them for support and accounting.

Messages you send us

If you use Help & support in the app to report a bug or request a skill or connector, we receive what you write, the app version, your email if you add it, and your phone model and Android version if you leave that option on. These are stored and emailed to us so we can reply and fix the problem. If you email or message us directly, we keep the conversation.

Web tools

Web search and page reading go through small servers we run on AWS, which pass your request on and return the result without storing it. If those are unavailable, search falls back to DuckDuckGo directly from your phone. YouTube search and downloads run from your phone, and downloaded media does not pass through our servers.

Diagnostics

The app includes Firebase Crashlytics and Firebase Analytics from Google, which receive crash reports and basic usage information such as app version and device model. Ultron also signs in to Firebase anonymously and uses Firebase App Check, so our servers can tell the request comes from the real app. Checking for app updates contacts our update server.

Sensitive permissions

Ultron can ask for the microphone, Accessibility, notification access, contacts, calendar, location, files, and usage access. Each is used only to carry out what you ask, and only after you turn on the matching connector and grant the permission. Accessibility lets Ultron read the screen, tap and type when you tell it to. You can switch any of these off in the app or in Android settings at any time.

Your choices

  • Turn connectors and permissions on or off whenever you like.
  • Delete memories, history, documents and usage data in the app.
  • Ask us to see, correct or delete the details we keep about you by writing to devxjitin@gmail.com. Deleting your details may mean we can no longer support or move your key.

Children

Ultron is not meant for children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

Changes

If we change this policy we will update the date above, and for significant changes we will tell customers by email or in the app.
